children: UK-based Indian-origin nurse receives USD 250,000 prize after emerging from more than 134,000 registrations across 214 countries and economies

Nurse Agimol Pradeep from the United Kingdom has been named the winner of the Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award 2026, receiving the USD 250,000 prize at a ceremony in Kochi on 12 September. Pradeep, a Senior Transplant Coordinator at King’s College Hospital and Honorary Senior Lecturer at the University of Salford, emerged as the winner from more than 134,000 registrations submitted by nurses across 214 countries and economies.

The award was presented by Shri V. D. Satheesan, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Keralam, alongside Dr. Azad Moopen, Founder and Executive Chairman, Aster DM Quality Care Ltd, Alisha Moopen, Executive Director, Aster DM Quality Care Ltd, T.J. Wilson, Director, Aster DM Quality Care, and Varun Khanna, Managing Director and Group CEO of Aster DM Quality Care Ltd.

The ceremony also featured a special message from Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the World Health Organization, who congratulated the finalists and recognised nurses’ contribution to healthcare worldwide.

Pradeep has focused her career on addressing healthcare inequities, particularly among minority communities. After identifying the impact of donor shortages on South Asian patients awaiting transplants, she co-founded the Upahaar initiative, which has registered more than 10,000 stem-cell donors.

“I have seen how a shortage of ethnically matched donors can leave patients from minority communities waiting longer for a life-saving transplant,” Pradeep said. She plans to use half of her prize money to expand organ and stem-cell donation initiatives through Upahaar, while also supporting nursing education and training.

Dr. Azad Moopen said Pradeep’s achievement reflects the “expertise, courage, compassion and unwavering commitment” that define exceptional nursing, adding that the award aims to recognise and elevate nurses’ contributions globally. Alisha Moopen highlighted Pradeep’s community-led work, saying her efforts in transplantation and organ donation among the UK’s South Asian community had “set a benchmark for many to follow.”

The remaining nine finalists were selected from Sweden, Saudi Arabia, Hong Kong SAR, India, Colombia, Namibia, Nigeria and Papua New Guinea. They included Dr. Aidah Alkaissi, Dinah Sevilla, Dr. Hammoda Abu-Odah, Hindumbi K, Johana Patricia Galvan Barrios, Josephine Nelago Angula, Oluchi Angel Okoi, Peter Fore and Ronald Mario Cañas Rojas.

The finalists underwent a selection process involving Ernst & Young LLP, a Screening Jury and a Grand Jury, with assessments based on professional achievement, leadership, innovation, impact and contributions to nursing.
Since its launch in 2021, the Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award has developed into an international platform celebrating nurses driving change across healthcare systems and communities.
